html:
Gonur Depe is the ruin of a Bronze Age town in the Murghab delta of Turkmenistan, lived in from about 2300 to 1600 BCE. It is the largest site of the Oxus civilisation.

The Soviet archaeologist Viktor Sarianidi dug there from 1972 for decades. He found a walled palace, temples, a royal cemetery with carts and animals buried with the dead, and a workshop quarter. Seals, ivory and pottery show trade with the Indus cities, Elam and Mesopotamia.

The site's fire altars led Sarianidi to argue that it was an early home of the faith later called Zoroastrianism, though many scholars doubt it. When the rivers shifted, the delta dried up and the town was left to the sands. The same delta later fed the city of Merv.
sum: Gonur Depe is the ruin of a Bronze Age town in the Murghab delta of Turkmenistan, lived in from about 2300 to 1600 BCE. It is the largest site of the Oxus civilisation.
